evidence.summary: K-dimension masking failure confirmed at runtime. Control K=128 (multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16, num_pid_k=8) reproduced the reference C = A @ dequant(B) exactly (max_abs_err=0.0 against ref_absmax=51.0). The tail case K=72 (legal 4-bit packing, 9 int32 rows, group_size=64 with a trailing partial group, num_pid_k=cdiv(72,16)=5) raised CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered. The 5th loop iteration loads g_idx/b/a for k in [72,80) with no K bounds mask (kernel.py:42-48), and the out-of-range g_idx then indexes scales/zeros at an arbitrary row, producing the fault. Zero codes were restricted to 0..14 so the c3 (zeros+1 wrap) question cannot confound this result.

rationale: Every load inside the k-loop is unmasked in the K dimension; only offs_am < M is masked. num_pid_k = cdiv(K, BLOCK_SIZE_K) rounds up, so a K that is a multiple of the packing factor 8 but not of 16 forces a full extra tile of out-of-range reads whose products are added to the accumulator. An out-of-range g_idx value also indexes scales/zeros arbitrarily.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract explicitly requires correct per-column group dequantization 'for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size, where the trailing partial group is still a group of its own.'

Host contract accepts a (M,K) with b_packed (K//(32//bits), N); BLOCK_SIZE_K is hardcoded to 16 and num_pid_k = cdiv(K,16), so any K in the admitted domain that is not a multiple of 16 triggers an unmasked tail iteration.

scope_rationale: problem.txt states the contract must hold "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size, where the trailing partial group is still a group of its own." K=72 with group_size=64 is exactly such a K, is a legal packing size for 4-bit (K/8 = 9 int32 rows per the wrapper docstring), and is admitted by the host signature. No test.py exists, so problem.txt is authoritative and I choose this representative K it explicitly admits.
statement: When K is not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16 (e.g. K=72 with 4-bit packing, group_size=64, so b_packed has 9 int32 rows and the trailing group is partial), the loop runs num_pid_k=cdiv(72,16)=5 iterations and the final iteration loads g_idx, b, scales, zeros and a for k in [72,80) with no K mask (lines 42-48 have no K bounds check). This reads past g_idx/b_packed and past each A row, so garbage (or out-of-range g_idx feeding an arbitrary scales/zeros row) is multiplied and accumulated into C, producing wrong output (or an illegal memory access) versus the reference C = A @ dequant(B).

evidence.summary: N-dimension masking did not produce an observable failure at runtime. With K=128 (multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16, so the confirmed c1 tail defect cannot confound) and zero codes restricted to 0..14 (c3 cannot confound), the N=64 control matched the reference exactly (max_abs_err=0.0, ref_absmax=30.88) and the N=48 tail case ALSO matched exactly (max_abs_err=0.0, ref_absmax=42.30; per-tile split: cols 0..31 err=0.0, cols 32..47 err=0.0). num_pid_n=cdiv(48,32)=2, so the second column tile did issue unmasked b/scales/zeros loads for offs_bn in [32,64) while only 48 columns exist, yet no CUDA illegal memory access occurred and the masked store (line 57) discarded the garbage columns. The over-read stays inside CUDA allocator slack for these sizes, so the unmasked N loads are a latent UB/portability concern rather than a demonstrated wrong-output or fault in this configuration. Claim as stated (fault or wrong (M,N) result) is rebutted for N=48; note it was never established as in_scope (scope=unknown).

rationale: Lines 32-35 build b/scales/zeros pointers from offs_bn with no offs_bn < N guard, and line 48/43/44 load them without a mask; only line 57 masks the store. Reading beyond the final row of a contiguous tensor has no guaranteed valid backing memory.
scope_rationale: problem.txt constrains the operator and explicitly generalizes over K, but says nothing about N divisibility, and there is no test.py/get_inputs pinning N. The host wrapper accepts arbitrary N, so the case is admitted by the signature, but I cannot show the benchmark domain requires a non-multiple-of-32 N; marking unknown rather than in_scope.
statement: When N is not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_N=32 (e.g. N=48), the loads of b (line 48), scales (line 43) and zeros (line 44) are unmasked in the N dimension while only the C store is masked, so the last column tile dereferences addresses past the end of b_packed/scales/zeros; this can raise a CUDA illegal memory access (or, for the qzeros word index offs_bn//8, read out-of-range packed data) rather than returning the correct (M,N) result.

data.expected_signal: Control (no zero code == 15) should match all-but-raw references identically. With zero codes == 15, the kernel should match the unwrapped `zeros+1` (=16) semantics with ~0 error and differ from the wrapped `(zeros+1)&maxq` (=0) reference by a large amount (~16*scale summed over K), which quantifies the deviation from upstream AutoGPTQ.
data.kernel_semantics_identified: zeros + 1 with no & maxq wrap (pre-wrap AutoGPTQ variant)
data.scope: unknown - intended zero-point convention not pinned by any artifact

evidence.summary: Behavioral divergence in c3 confirmed at runtime with K=128/N=64 (so the confirmed c1 K-tail defect and the c2 N-tail case cannot confound). Control with no zero code == 15: kernel matched BOTH the unwrapped (zeros+1) and wrapped ((zeros+1)&15) references exactly (err 0.0 for both, since the two agree when no code is 15), and differed from the literal problem.txt 'zero, no +1' reference by 3.86 (ref_absmax 35.47) — i.e. the kernel definitively implements a +1 zero-point offset, not the literal problem.txt formula. With all zero codes == 15 (128/128 codes): kernel matched the unwrapped zeros+1 (=16) reference exactly (err 0.0) and differed from the upstream AutoGPTQ wrapped (zeros+1)&maxq (=0) reference by max_abs 45.42 against ref_wrapped_absmax 33.65 (>100% relative). Mixed case (44/128 codes == 15): err_vs_unwrapped 0.0, err_vs_wrapped 78.81 vs ref_wrapped_absmax 44.21. So line 46's missing `& maxq` is a real, large behavioral difference from upstream AutoGPTQ whenever a packed zero nibble is maxq, exactly as claimed. Which convention is contractually required is still not decided by this probe: problem.txt states plain `zero` with no +1 at all, so the kernel deviates from the literal spec formula in every configuration (including zero-code-free ones), while it exactly reproduces the pre-wrap AutoGPTQ variant. Scope for c3 remains 'unknown' — no test.py or reference implementation exists to fix the intended zero-point convention.

rationale: Current AutoGPTQ applies `zeros = (zeros + 1) & maxq`; this port drops the mask. Randomly generated qzeros will contain the code 15 with probability ~1/16 per (group, column), so a benign random probe will hit the case, but only if the reference used for comparison implements the wrapping semantics.
scope_rationale: problem.txt's stated formula is (unpacked_q[k,n] - zero[g_idx[k],n]) * scale[g_idx[k],n] with no stated +1 or wrap convention, so which of {zero, zero+1, (zero+1)&maxq} is contractually required is ambiguous without the reference implementation; scope is unknown until the intended zero-point convention is clarified.
statement: Line 46 computes `zeros = zeros + 1` without the `& maxq` wrap, so when a packed zero-point nibble equals maxq (15 for 4-bit) the kernel dequantizes with zero=16 instead of the wrapped value 0, giving dequant values that differ from the reference by exactly 16*scale for every k in that group and column.
